prerequisites: Familiarity with indispensable elements of mathematical analysis and calculus (derivations, integrations, and limits of functions of one or more variables).

learning_outcomes.text: The student acquires and consolidates the basic concepts of general physics in the language of mathematical analysis, of vector and integral calculus.
Acquires the scientific-technical methodology required to deal with the problems of physics in quantitative terms, with particular regard to classical mechanics.

syllabus_topics: Mathematical introduction and basic vector algebra
Elements of probability and theory of statistics
Differential calculus: gradient, divergence and curl of a vector field
Vector integral calculus: line integral and circulation of a vector field
Application to the kinematics of particle systems: the main formula of rigid body kinematics
Kinematics of relative motions: transformation of displacements, velocities and accelerations
Dynamics: Active and vinculum forces, static measurement of forces
Elements of statics (main equations, center of mass) and on friction phenomena
First and second law of dynamics
Applications to the dynamics of rigid bodies
Conservation of linear and angular momentum
Center of mass and its properties
Work and energy: Work of one force and of a system of forces
Work done by the weight force
Conditions satisfied by a conservative field of force
Law of universal gravitation: Keplero laws, Newton's law on gravitation
Acceleration of gravity on the surface of the earth
teaching_methods: Frontal lessons in classroom introducing theoretical aspects
Application of notions and resolution of exercises
Visual integrative tools based on projector slide projections
assessment_rules: The examination consists of a final one-hour written test and a further oral exam. To be admitted to the oral examination, a positive judgment (score >= 18/30) must be achieved in the written exam. The final mark is calculated as the arithmetic average, rounded up, of the written and oral examination marks.
